utterances.text: Do you recall any -- in the second sentence, it says: "For a long period of time, I have been facing problems with enduring this profession." Do you have any recollection of what the problems were that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely I remember. When you said "personal problems," personal problems means family problems, but I also was examined in the centre -- health centre in Split. I had a condition, I had a high blood pressure and heart problems, and I didn't want to seek treatment within the brigade. So I decided to write this request and ask to be relieved of my professional duties within the 4th Guards Brigade --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 1st Split Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, from the time you began your compulsory military service in 1993, I believe, until your departure from the 4th Guards Brigade, is it true that you had been subjected to disciplinary measures four times for abandoning your unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall any disciplinary measures being imposed because we were stationed in Crvana Luka near Pakostenje [phoen]. And it didn't involve absence without leave as you implied, but, rather my going out in the evening while on leave, where as I extended the hours of my leave or it was not approved beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Still within this document, Mr. Registrar, I think I'm looking for a document 10 September 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, would you like to tender the other document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is all part of the same e-court document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is all part of the same e-court, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Next page, page 4, of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If could you read that document, Mr. Gojanovic. This is now during the period of time where he were serving as a conscript. It's dated 10 September 1993. If you read below the part that says, "Statement," it specifically says: "The person named above arbitrarily abandoned the unit on 5 September 1993 and returned on 6 September 1993." Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall being meted out, confinement in military prison lasting three days?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn, Mr. Registrar, to page 7 of this document. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, that's the wrong one. 1D22-0378. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you could take a look at this document, Mr. Gojanovic, it's dated 13 April 1994. This is now while you are a member of the 4th Guards Brigade. It's a disciplinary measured issued by Brigadier Zamir Krsticevic. Again, you will note that it says you were disciplined a second time for arbitrarily abandoning your unit on 26 March 1994. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you ever recall receiving a reduction in pay of 10 percent for one month?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next document is page 8, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, this is a document dated 15 July 1994, again while you were a member of the 4th Guards Brigade. It's a third disciplinary measure again signed by Brigadier-General Krsticevic. If you could read that over, please, it says you, again, arbitrarily abandoned your unit, 12 June, 1994. Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And based on your prior answer, I assume that you do not recall -- actually, let me change it. It is a different disciplinary measure. You received a reduction in salary of 10 per cent for three months now. Do you recall that disciplinary measure being meted out?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next one, please: 8 September 1994; 1D22-0368.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you could take a look at that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Page 6 of the English, I'm sorry, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is your fourth disciplinary measure. Again, it says you're being disciplined because of the fact that on 23 July 1994, you arbitrarily abandoned your unit, although you were assign to the guard service. As we can note, the discipline against you is escalating. You are now being having your salary reduced 20 per cent for one month. Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't recall that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall ever having your pay reduced by 20 per cent?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask to have this marked, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D190, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D190 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have some questions regarding your participation in the 113th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the registrar to call up 1D22-0147.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a document prepared by the commander of the 113th Brigade, Mr. Kotlar. He was asked to put together a roster of the participants of the 113th Brigade -- I should say the soldiers of the 113th who participated in Operation Storm. Can you see that? It is dated 21 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Commander Kotlar, and have I a hard copy for you which I will give to you, together a roster of 2.237 soldiers of the 113th Brigade, and your name is not on there. So I would ask you to check for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I also have one for the Bench, if the Bench wishes to look through the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And I would ask you if you have an explanation for why are you not identified by Commander Kotlar as having participated with the 113th during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have an explanation because it is not my fault, but I received a medal for Operation Storm from the 4th Split Brigade as if I had been in the area of Dubrovnik. I never went to collect the medal because I thought that if I had not been in that area, I cannot receive a medal from the 4th Split Brigade, in which I did not participate during Operation Storm. At that time, I was a member of the 113th Brigade. If I'm not recorded here, I don't think it is my fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, the medal you received was actually a medal that was issued in 2000 by President Mesic, subsequently, for your participation in Operation Storm in the 4th Guards Brigade, according to the description for why you got the medal. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You never received a medal between 1995 and 2000 for any participation as a member of the 113th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that the document be marked and admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole of the document is including the list attached. Let me just check.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is 78 pages, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, to have 78 pages of names in evidence, is this not a matter which the parties could easily agree upon whether the name of this witness appears on the list, yes or no, and perhaps at one page, because the copy takes half a wood to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will discuss it with the Prosecution during the next break, and see if there can be a stipulation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps, we mark the document for identification, and I strongly suggest to the parties that either they agree on the matter or that the admission into evidence would be limited to the cover page, which sets out the what the list of names is about and then perhaps the first page, just as an example of how this list was prepared.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D191, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I request a clarification from Mr. Misetic regarding the last question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you don't understand the question, you can. The last question was - let me just have a look - a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's line 12 and 13 on page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. Yes. If the question is not clear to you, please tell us what is not clear. If, however, the question is clear to you, I would like you to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is not clear to me is this: Does Mr. Misetic believe that I got the medal, or that it was never awarded to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was not about whether a medal was awarded to you, but whether you received a medal between 1995 and 2000 for your participation as a member of the 113th; so not medals for other activities, but whether you did receive or did not receive. The suggestion that you did not receive it for your activities in the 113th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. I can confirm that. I did not receive any medals for activity in the 113th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could call up 1D22-0350.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, in addition to the fact that Commander Kotlar did not include you on the roster of participants of the 113th in Operation Storm, on the 3rd of September, 1995, he actually sent a request to the military police to find you and have you brought to the unit. I'd ask to you take a look at that, and your name is listed at number 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, I think it's on the next page of the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, probably. First of all, I don't remember this document. I had never seen it before. Second, I was never aware of this fact. Third, in my records, there was one address and I lived at another address, and that's probably the reason why I am on this list. The military police never came to get me, and I'm certain about that. I wouldn't have forgotten it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, if you were actually in your unit, it wouldn't matter what your house address was, would it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before that, I was in the 4th Split Brigade, and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you were in your unit on or about the 3rd of September, 1995, Commander Kotlar would not have had issue a request for your apprehension regardless of what your home address is. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until then, I wasn't even in the 113th Brigade, before the mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, the date of the document is the 3rd of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, I was mobilised into the 113th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Had you not been mobilised --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that, I had demobed from the 4th Split Brigade, and there was an interval of more than a month between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure where our miscommunication is here, sir. Paragraph 3 your statement says, you were mobilised to join the 113th Sibenik Reserve Brigade on the 2nd of August 1995. This is it a document dated 3rd of September 1995 --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- a month later where they are seeking your apprehension to bring you to the unit. And in addition to that, Commander Kotlar on the 21st of August does not include you on a list of over 2000 members who participated in Storm. So I'm asking you if you can explain this to us.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat again the relevant date, the date which is in dispute? You said 3rd September 1995, about forceable mobilisation and the bringing me in. This is not possible. I don't know what this means. This is totally incomprehensible to me. I had been mobilised in the 113th, prior to this, for the Operation Storm. After that, I was demobilised. I don't know what this is about. This is completely incomprehensible, the date and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you were demobilised, according to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can check that with the military department. You can get the exact date because you had the documents of the military department. I told you a moment ago I didn't spend much time with the 113th Brigade, just in the Operation Storm and a short time before that. After that, I was demobilised. I don't think anything about this document, and I can't us understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, at the same time where you are challenging the official documents that are put to you, you, instead of answering Mr. Misetic's question, refer to official documents. Apparently, there seems to be some confusion. So, therefore, would you please answer the question when you demobilised from the 113th Brigade. That was the question that was put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You did not allow me the time or the possibility to look up my own documentation and find the date when I was demobilised. I was not prepared for this. As far as this document is concerned, it is not a document from the military department. The only authorative document can be from the military department, and it would be the one from the military police. This one is from the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to keep matters simple. In your statement, you say you were mobilised on the 2nd of August in the 113th. Now, apart from the fact that you were not reported as someone to be decorated as having participated in Operation Storm on the 16th of August, and apart from the fact that your name appears on a list of the 3rd of September to be brought to your unit, tell us how long were you active in the 113th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I was active for a little other a month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would bring us close to the 3rd of September. You have written this note about being relieved of your military duties, which is a note without a date. Do you remember when you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is related to his service in the 4th Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, the 4th. Then I'm mistake there. Perhaps, Mr. Misetic, you can give follow-up on how he left the 113th. Yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We'd like to make clear, Your Honour, that the handwritten note was from 1994 and was his request to leave the 4th Gaurds Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although, it doesn't bear a date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It does have a date. Unfortunately, it is cut off in the copy that we got. On the official record, it says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, for me, it has no date, but the original has a date. The Chamber always prefers to have the full copy. You may notice that I was looking for a date, as you may have noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And I also need to clarify this is not a military police document. It is a document in front of you, sir, of Commander Kotlar, as the author of the document, who is sending it to the military police requesting that --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea what that is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what the Presiding Judge is interested to know, which is the circumstances surrounding your eventual demobilisation or, perhaps more broadly, your departure from the 113th. Can you explain the circumstances under which you ultimately left the 113th?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. I left the 113th Brigade after the completion of Operation Storm. I left, in fact, several days after Operation Storm was finished because we rotated in shifts in Donji Srb. And after a month, like most people who participated in the operation, I requested that I be demobilised. That's the whole story.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall ever being apprehended by the military police in September of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. I have absolutely no recollection of that. Nobody brought me in, nobody apprehended me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm prepared to move on to another subject, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You repeatedly said that this is a document originating from Commander Kotlar, I think. I have not found that yet on the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If there is one more page -- up top you, you see the heading where it is coming from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The 113th Brigade HV, Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You related to a person, but it is related to a unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If can I have this marked and tendered, Your Honour, then I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D192, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D192 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, let's go through your statement in the events that you took about in that statement, and let's go back to paragraph 7 of your statement, 2005. You recall this morning I asked you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's on page 4 of the English, Your Honours, towards the bottom. There is a reference to a tank commander being considered with his commander for this mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This morning, sir, I asked you to identify that commander, and you were able to give his name. You said his nickname was Sudac. I asked you whether Radoslav Juricev was familiar. You agreed.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would like to call up 1D22-0088. That is a witness statement obtained by the Gotovina Defence of Radoslav Juricev. All of the statements that I'm about to show you are notarized and signed. If we could go to the next page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I wish to seek a clarification from the Defence counsel as to whether he is intending to put statements made by witnesses the Defence team has interviewed, who we don't know whether they would be here to testify, to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Depending on his answers to the questions, we're prepared to call the witnesses, if necessary. At this point, I would like to confront him, though, with the statements of the people who participated in these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, it depends on the results apparently, which sounds rather logical, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I will see how it goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that. You said that the witness confirmed the name. I think he said, "I think." Yes. So it is not a real firm confirmation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You used the nickname Sudac, and I don't know if caught on the first that Mr. Juricev identified his own nickname as Sudac. I'd ask you to read that statement, paragraphs 4 and 5. At paragraph 5, Mr. Juricev, Sudac, says explicitly: "I know every man who was with me. I am certain that Vladimir Gojanovic was neither assigned to me, nor that he was driving in my tank. I am certain that he wasn't at the tanks in Gornje Bicane either." And you will note at paragraph 7, he actually describes the axis of attack that you identify in your statement at paragraph 7, about the tank group heading towards Sonkovici?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Which question --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... is it possible, sir, that, in fact, you were not part of the tank group that went on the attack towards Sonkovici?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's not possible. I was on that tank, but it is a fact that Sudac and I did not know each other at the time. It is quite natural that at that moment, since he didn't know me, he simply didn't register me like I didn't register many other people and didn't know their names. It was only after the war that I practically met with Sudac, officially.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 13 of his statement, I take your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 13 of his statement, which is on the next page, Mr. Registrar. Once again, Your Honour, I notice that it says confidential privileged on the top. However, I waive it on all these statements, and I will ensure that it doesn't happen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "During the combat activities in Operation Storm, I didn't see the current chairman of the HURBDR, Vladimir Gojanovic. He wasn't with me or in my unit." I understand the point you made, though, in your answer, sir, so let me move on to the next portion of your statement, which is the story about you assisting a wounded individual. That is in paragraph 6 of your statement, the last sentence. I asked you this morning to identify either the person that was killed or the person that was wounded. You said you didn't know the names. Let me first show you a document at tab 5, so we can identify for the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, before we move on, what is your intention as far as the statement of a person nicknamed Sudac is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If necessary, Your Honour, we will call him in the Defence case, if the Court wants. I am, obviously, going to tender the statement and ask that it be moved in evidence, and I will leave it in the hands of the Court to decide what you wish to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we have, of course, a potential problem in the field of 92 bis, 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to invite, while it is now on the record, that you tender it. I think the document should be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I invite the parties to see whether there is any practical way of resolving this, either to put it in a different way in the record; because if we would admit this into evidence, then it would be most likely the whole of the document, without the possibility for the Prosecution to cross-examine this person on these matters. If this is a practical way of agreeing of, for example, agreeing that a statement was given to I don't know exactly to whom, but to the Defence, which says, and then limit ourselves to the portions you read to the witness; then I think for the purposes of this moment, that might be enough, but I leave it to the parties at this moment to see whether they can reach a procedural agreement on how to deal with this document. If not, of course, then the Chamber will decide the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just for the record, so we don't spend time on this later, I have several such statement. I will agree with the procedure Your Honour has just laid out, and I will attempt to work out some agreement with the Prosecution and see if we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you already could take care that those portions which are of core relevance for your questioning, that you read them out literally perhaps, so that at least we have that on the record, which might facilitate solutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D193, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could call up --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: As I said before, Mr. Gojanovic, I would like to show you the official documents about the dead and the two injured in the 113th in the incident to which you refer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, it's 1D22-0036.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a report from Commander Kotlar, reporting on casualties suffered by the 113th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you'll see the name Davor Perisa and the description of the wounding incident which seems to match up with the description in your statement at paragraph 6. It says: "This person was shot through his left upper leg while participating in an attack on Gracac in the village of Pavasovici. So one of the individuals was Davor Perisa?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The second individual is identified as Boris Filipovic. Again, the description is on 4 August 1995 in the village of Pavasovici: "During the attack of the HV 113th, the enemy fired at our targets; and at one point, the soldier referred to above was shot through his right lower leg." Again, it is signed by Commander Kotlar. Third page, this is now the diseased. His name was Boris Garma, and you will note that your description of how he was killed differs from description given by Commander Kotlar. You say, at paragraph 7, that he was killed -- was hit by a bullet and killed. Commander Kotlar says: "On 4 August 1995, during the attack on Gracac, on the way between Pavasovici and Gracac, the soldier referred to above was killed. The enemy employed every available weapon and pieces. At one point, a mortar mine impacted two metres from Boris Garma, and killed him on the spot."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me take you now to the statements of the two wounded individuals, Mr. Perisa and Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would asked that this be marked and tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D194, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D194 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next document, Mr. Registrar, is 1D22-0097. It is it the witness statement of Davor Perisa taken by the Gotovina Defence. It is a witness statement dated 9 May 2008. The next page, Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At paragraph 2: During Operation Storm, I was a member of the 3rd Battalion of the 113th Infantry Brigade." I would first ask you to take note of the fact that the witness says he was a member of the 3rd Battalion, not the 2nd Battalion, as you say you in your statement, that you were a member of. Paragraph 4: "On 4 August 1995, at around 0900 hours, I was wounded from an infantry weapon. " Paragraph 5: "I was rescued by the men who were around me." Paragraph 6: "The men who rescued me bear the surname Bratic. One was from Sonkovici, the other Pira Martovsi [phoen]. I do not recall Vladimir Gojanovic being present or helping getting me out. I only recall the aforementioned men by the surname Bratic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will ask him a question after I show him the second statement, Your Honour. I think it would be probably appropriate that I have this marked, which is consistent with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is one of the documents just to be marked for identification, Ms. Mahindaratne. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D195, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The second statement, Mr. Registrar, is 1D22-0121.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You will note on this one, Mr. Gojanovic, this is the statement of Boris Filipovic, one of the two men injured. The statement is dated 9 May, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we can turn the page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, in paragraph 2, please note: "During Operation Storm, I was a member of the 3rd Battalion, 3rd Company. The commander of the company was Dragan Rak. I occupied the post of platoon commander in that company." Paragraph 3: "On 4 August 1995, I was at the front line ready for the commencement of the operation. That day, I was wounded at around 0900 hours. I suffered a gunshot wound from an infantry weapon. At place in time that I was wounded, I was surrounded by people I knew. Vladimir Gojanovic was not among them. I am certain that I was rescued by the members of my platoon, who were originally from Bradisa, a settlement I come from as well. These persons were Bozo, Saro, Covo, Ive, Babic. These men were with me throughout the war."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for the record, we left the it in the statement the way the witness said the names. He said he did not recall the surnames of the individuals. That is why I did not wish to suggest to him any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First, Mr. Gojanovic, on paragraph 4, are you ever referred to by anyone as any of the following names: Bozo, Saro, Covo, Ive, or Babic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Covo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, no. Did you ever go by the nickname of Bozo, Saro, Covo, Ive, or Babic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nor could anyone call me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that this are be marked for identification as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if may address you as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think my microphone is [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to put it on the record. It seems to me that I take that you do not object against the document to be marked for identification? If you're not, then I will put that on the record as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I want to say that I would object to it being tendered, but certainly not to be marked as identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the only thing Mr. Misetic requested. So this is the third now in a row of documents, marked for identification, subject to further discussions between the parties. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D196, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will show you one more --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we have the break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any specific reason for that, because we usually go on for another 20 minutes. But if you say you need a sanitary stop, it's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Toilet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have a break now and resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, I showed you two of the statements -- the two statements of the two individuals who were actually wounded by Pavasovici, which you describe in your statement at paragraph 6. Both of them declare that they have no recollection of you being present. Is it possible, sir, that, in fact, you were not present at the time that these two soldiers were wounded and evacuated?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, you showed the document a minute ago, a little while ago, which showed that there was an individual who was killed and there were four or five wounded soldiers in that operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, the question simply is: "Is it possible that you were not present at that event?" It's not a time to start arguing with Mr. Misetic, but it is a question. Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I will provide the answer. It is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, next I want to discuss --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, the microphone is switched off.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A number of microphones for the whole of the courtroom is limited to five. I'll switch mine off.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Misetic suggested to the witness that he was shown two statements of the two individuals who were actually wounded. Now what we saw here were two statements of two people who claim they were wounded in this incident. As to whether they are the actual casualties, the persons who were wounded and whom Mr. Gojanovic heard we don't know that. It is not a fact so far, which is where we got the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was a strong suggestion in Mr. Misetic's question that these were the same persons as described by the witness, and it was put in that way to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe, before I put the statements in, I gave the official report of the commander of the 113th Brigade, where he identifies the casualties by name and the individual incidents at Pavosovic, which is where we got the names of the individuals

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, Ms. Mahindaratne says it is not a fact, but it's what someone claims to be fact. I mean, these are official documents. I couldn't say that I have never seen documents that did not fully reflect the truth. I'm not saying or not suggesting that this is the case, but Ms. Mahindaratne is right; and, at the same time, we are in a situation where it was totally appropriate for you to put it in this way to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your statement, you say you were a member of the 2nd Battalion of the 113th, and this is at paragraph 6 of your statement, right at the beginning: "Our axis of attack was towards Sonkovici, and just one battalion, namely, the 2nd Battalion, was involved on that axis of attack." You go on to the top of the next page, and it says: "The battalion consisted of about 100 men and had artillery support." Now, sir, just as a preliminary matter, how many men are in a battalion?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A battalion can number up to 200 to 300 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this axis of attack, in your statement that you as a member of the 2nd Battalion participated, and I believe your statement is clear that just one battalion participated, I'd like to show you a statement of the commander of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could please call up 1D22-0072. It is the statement of the commander of the 3rd Battalion, 113th Guards Brigade, Dragan Rak, R-a-k. This is a statement taken 8 May 2008. If we could go to the next page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Right at the beginning, he says: "This is a voluntary statement concerning my participation in Operation Storm during which I was commander of the 3rd Infantry Battalion of the 113th Brigade, which consisted of reserve members who were mobilised for Operation Storm?" And the third paragraph: "At approximately 05:00 hours, we launched our attack from our initial positions from Pavasovici towards Gracac and Sonkovici. Due to the heavy enemy resistance from Sonkovici mainly by use of anti-air guns and mortar guns, our attack decreased in pace; and after the death of soldier Boris Garma, and wounded soldiers Boris Filipovic and Davor Perisa, offensive operations were halted. We proceeded to withdraw our soldiers and take care of our wounded."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Last paragraph beginning with the second sentence: "I know Vladimir Gojanovic personally from 1992 or 1993 when he was a conscript member of the 113th Brigade, but I never saw him during Operation Storm, nor did I see him during the remainder of the events described in this statement." First question, sir, is: The 2nd Battalion of the 113th did not go on the attack towards Sonkovici. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can provide an answer that would not confine -- be confined to yes or no, because I have to explain a very delicate fact. According to the statement of this witness, I was a member of the 113th Brigade and that this witness knew me at this time. According to the documents by -- provided by the Defence council Mr. Mikulicic, it is claimed that I was never a member of the 113th Brigade. So I think that this statement of this witness is totally illegitimate. On the other hand, the most important fact that I would like to point out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether legitimate or not is not for a witness to decide. Your comments, because it is comments on others rather than answering the question of Mr. Misetic, might not be fully correct where you said that these documents showed that you never were. I think what the documents, at least as I understood them, was that you never participated on -- or you were not reported on the 16th of August to have participated as an active member of the 113th; and that on the 3rd of September, that they were trying to get you to your unit, which is not the same as what you tell us now. So, please, answer the question, not necessarily with a yes or no, but without further comment the on what others said. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you need me to repeat the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The 2nd Battalion of the 113th Brigade did not conduct an attack towards Sonkovici. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, it was the 2nd Battalion. But you have to take into account that I had just been mobilised and that I practically did not really know the exact number of my battalion, nor did I know the men or they me. So you have to keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So, now, is it your testimony, sir, that, in fact, you don't know which battalion you belonged to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the circumstances, it is possible that I misnamed the battalion, that I used the wrong number, because I was mobilised on that day and went into action. So I didn't know the men or the number of the battalion, but I know for certain that this was a battalion that was mobilised -- the reserve forces that were mobilised. The first two battalions did not do this. And this 3rd Battalion of the 113th which was the one where the -- which was the one that included the mobilised reservists before the action, that was the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You were not under the command of Commander Rak, were you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know personally the commanders above me, except the ones that I already mentioned in my statement. How could I know when I was there for the first time on the first day? It was as if I was dropped from a helicopter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, would you allow me one clarifying question. In 1992 and 1993, were you, because I don't see that in paragraph 2 of the statement, were you a conscript member of the 113th Brigade? In your statement you say that, in November 1993, you joined the 4th Guards Brigade. But prior to that, were you ever a member of the 113th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness, based on that answer, isn't it true that you did not serve your compulsory military service in the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it true that I did not serve my cull sore military service in the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And it isn't true, that as a result of that, you had to actually serve your compulsory service in 1993 in the Croatian army. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And before you could get to the 4th Guards Brigade, you had to serve your compulsory service in the brigade of your local area, which was the 113th Sibenik Brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Where did you serve your compulsory military service?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My initial training was in Sinj; and then I was reassigned to Zagreb, specialised to anti-nuclear, biological, and chemical warfare; and then following this, I was in a specialised brigade for professional soldiers. Let me just try to recall the place where this was. This was the centre for professional military training in Delnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And what unit were you a formally a part of when you were doing your training in Sinj?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sinj, there was a centre for basic training and that falls under the Sinj area, the Sinj Brigade. After that, I was transferred to Zagreb for two months where I was a member of a unit attached to the anti-chemical, biological, and nuclear warfare. And after that, I went to the centre for training of professional brigades. And after that, I was assigned to the 4th, which means that before Operation Storm, I was never a member of the 113th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I need to mark this one for identification as well, the statement of Dragan Rak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Mahindaratne, I take it that you do not object against having it marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D197, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to show you -- you have now testified that it was possible that you were actually a member of the 3rd Battalion moving towards Sonkovici. So I'd like to show you two more statements quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, this is 1D22-0313.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a statement of Srecko Grubisic, deputy commander of the 2nd Company of the 3rd Infantry Battalion of the 113th. A witness statement dated 8 May 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At paragraph 2, deputy commander Grubisic states: "During Operation Storm, I was deputy commander of the 2nd Company of the 3rd Infantry Battalion of the 113th Brigade." At paragraph 5, he again describes the wounding incident, and says: "As we did not have artillery support, we withdrew to the village of Pavasovici. During our withdrawal, Davor Perisa was wounded. There was one company from the 1st Battalion which withdrew the wounded Perisa. Next statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I could have this marked for identification as well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D198, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It keeps that status.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Before I move on to the next statement, let me read to you what he says at paragraph 10: "As deputy commander of the company, I did not see Vladimir Gojanovic during any of these activities, nor during the conduction of the operation. Considering Gojanovic served in a guards brigade and finished specialised guards brigade training, I'm sure we would have made him section commander had he been there. The recruiting office would surely have indicated that a man who completed guards brigade training was entering our unit." Actually, I did want to ask you this question, because this is why I asked you this question first this morning. You agreed with me that, as someone wearing -- if you were wearing the uniform of the 4th Guards Brigade, you would have been conspicuous to people. Can you offer us an explanation for why commanders of the 3rd Battalion don't -- might not recognise you or recall you being a participant in these activities?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My explanation is that nobody knew me. None of these people knew me because I had just been mobilised into their brigade on the eve of that operation. I wore a uniform that was rather special, relative to infrared rays. What was conspicuous about it was that, on the left chest sleeve, I still had the insignia of the 4th Split Brigade, but I had no insignia whatsoever on the sleeve, either of the 113th or the 4th. But they probably did not notice any of that because everybody had their hands full just before the operation; plus, we had no line-ups of that kind, and it was not logical to appoint a newcomer to be a section commander or a platoon commander. I think that logic is understandable even to those who had never been in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could call up 1D22-0321. This is the statement of Jordan Tudic, deputy commander of the 3rd Infantry Battalion of the 113th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned -- when I asked for names this morning, you mention as nickname of Covo. Do you know if that was Mr. Tudic's nickname was Covo?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So now we're talking about --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we are talking about that same person, the one from Brodarica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at what he says. This is his statement to the Gotovina Defence dated 8 May 2008. Paragraph 2, Mr. Tudic, Covo, says: "During Operation Storm, I was deputy commander of the 3rd Infantry Battalion of the 113th Brigade." If we go down to paragraph 7, towards the middle of the paragraph: "I decided to halt further breaching. I deployed my men into the ditch and hills from the village of Pavasovici to the village or Gracac. And then to paragraph 8, second sentence: "As a result, Boris Filipovic was wounded. Some ten minutes after him being wounded, I approached him. At that point, a group of soldiers were with me by the names of Govic, Alen; Babic, Bozo; Tudic, Ivica. When I approached the wounded soldier, I determined he had been wounded in the leg, and I then organised his withdrawal on a tent canvass with the help of a group of soldiers. "I declare that Vladimir Gojanovic was not present during the withdrawal of this wounded soldier. Gojanovic was known to me from before, and I would have surely noticed him had he been there." At paragraph 13: "Concerning I personally led all offensive operations from Skradin to Drvar, I surely would have noticed the soldier, Vladimir Gojanovic, had he been present in those areas." Now, you, in your witness statement, describe the withdrawal of the wounded soldier on a tent, and this morning you gave us the name -- nickname Covo, which you say now say at least likely to be Mr. Tudic. Is it possible, sir, that, in fact, you were not a member of the 3rd Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you again, with full responsibility, that it is it not possible that I was not a member of that battalion in that operation. I say with full responsibility that I only noticed Covo after I crossed the first minefield together with a group of ten volunteers. I crossed it on top of a tank together with Sudac. Then I saw him again in the follow-up action of mopping up the terrain; whereas, you are talking about the previous day and the wounding when I had not yet noticed Covo. What I remember is that I first noticed him the next day, and Covo did not join that group of ten volunteer. I saw him later in the action of mopping up the terrain which involved a larger number of troupes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I would ask that this be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same procedure, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D199, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Let me turn next to 1D22-0052.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is now a statement provided by the assistant commander of the political activity department of the 2nd Battalion of the HV 113th Brigade, which is what in your statements you say you were a part of. His name is Josko Babacic, and this is a statement dated 8 May 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2: "I was assistant commander of the political activity department of the 2nd Battalion of the HV 113th Brigade. The 2nd Infantry Battalion was comprised of conscripts." Page 4 -- paragraph 4, I apologise: "From these positions, we commenced the operation towards the villages of Cista Velika and Cista Mala." Let me stop right there. Do you recall, perhaps, being part of an operation towards Cista Velika or Cista Mala, if you know where those places are?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I certainly did not participate in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 5: "During preparations for the operation, according to a written order by the brigade commander, preparations were conducted with all soldiers, officers, and non-commissioned officers, regarding treatment of prisoners of war and wounded enemy soldiers and civilians, which I conducted personally with the help of a psychologist in our brigade, Marina Gulin, who can confirm this fact." Paragraph 6: "During preparations, all soldiers received a booklet on conduct in accordance with the Geneva Conventions." Paragraph 9, now this is where Mr. Babacic is talking about whether or not you were present with the 2nd Battalion. He says, towards the bottom of paragraph 9: "Vladimir Gojanovic was not amongst the soldiers we encountered, and I am sure that I would have recognised him considering I know him personally. Gojanovic is extremely tall, and I would have surely seen him had he been there. As I said, I know him personally." Paragraph 13: "As assistant commander of the political activity department and as former commander of the recon company, and having commanded units during the operation, I often communicated with other commanders, lead takeovers of units and positions, and I can say with certainty that I did not see Vladimir Gojanovic as a member of any unit." Now, I want to discuss, because we discussed yesterday, your information that may have been given to you prior to or in the course of Operation Storm concerning proper treatment of civilians and prisoners of war referenced in this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Before I do that, I'd like to show another document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This would be, Mr. Registrar, 65 ter 1532. First, if I could ask that this be marked for identification, this statement that is before us, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be marked for identification as Exhibit D200.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gojanovic, what is on your screen now is a portion of General Gotovina's attack order for Operation Storm from the 2nd of August, 1995, and it's an order that goes to the political activities department.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, Mr. Registrar. Back. There. Right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At number 6, General Gotovina orders the political activities department, and it says one of the tasks is familiarizing units with the need -- Actually, let me start at number 5: Familiarising members with conduct in occupied settlements and handling of war booty. Number 6: Familiarising units with the need to eliminate all negative occurrences that will surface in the course of combat operations and with a focus on preventing, torching, and destruction of larger populated areas and towns. Number 8: Advising members of units on conduct with civilians and POWs in according with the Geneva Convention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, Mr. Registrar. If we can go to the next page, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Number 6 is organising carry of dead, wounded, and infirm. Now, sir, that was the order of General Gotovina on the 2nd of August to the political activity department. We've now seen a statement from Mr. Babacic, assistant commander of the political activity department of the 2nd Battalion of the HV 113th Brigade; and he says, as part of the order he received through the chain of command, that, in fact, preparations concerning the proper treatment of soldiers and civilians was conducted and that all soldiers received a booklet on conduct in accordance with the Geneva Convention? Do you recall receiving such a booklet?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tell me, please, are you talking about Mr. Babacic, who was the commander of the 2nd Battalion? That's what you said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I said the document, the statement says he was assistant commander of the political activity department of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And we have established that, according to these participants, I was in the 3rd Battalion on the Sonkovic-Gracac line. Now you are asking me about the political activity service of the 2nd Battalion, and I was not a member of that battalion, neither according to Mr. Babacic, nor in accordance with my own recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Gojanovic, I'm asking you these questions because, quite frankly, I'm not sure what we're established, and your statement says you were in the 2nd Battalion. So what I'd like to know, regardless of whether it was done by Mr. Babacic -- and I will remind you of your testimony, yesterday, that there was some discussion after Operation Storm started according to you, and I can read it. Actually, this is the transcript, page 2873 -- I'm sorry, page 2940, lines 6 through 11. Judge Orie had asked you a question: "Were you under instructions to deal with what you called civilians this way?" Your answer: "We were issued brief instructions relating to the civilian population, to the effect that their security should be ensured and that casualties should be prevented in the course of the military operation." Now, the question is: Isn't it true that the political activities branch of the 113th Guards Brigade, regardless of the battalion, in fact passed down General Gotovina's order about proper treatment of civilians and POWs?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for my experience, I did not receive a booklet about Geneva Conventions as you mentioned here. I stand by the statement I gave and that you have just read.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's put the booklet aside for a second. I'm asking about the instructions. Isn't it true that the political activities branch of the 113th Brigade, regardless of which battalion, in fact passed down General Gotovina's order about proper treatment of civilians and POWs? I base this on your claim that you received instructions relating to the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that is an unfair question. I don't know how this witness -- whether he received or not is another question. But as to whether whatever he received passed down from General Gotovina downwards at his level, he would not be aware of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has stated that he received the instruction. We have a statement that the political activities branch, in fact, at least in the 2nd Battalion, passed the instruction, and he says he received instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But do we know whether the witness has any knowledge by which channels the instructions came to him? That appears to be the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will remove the part about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask it this way: Isn't it true that it was the political activities department, of whatever battalion you say you were in, that issued these instructions that you referred to yesterday in your answer to Judge Orie?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the second part of the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat the whole question to you. Isn't it true that it was the political activities department, of whatever battalion you say you were in, that issued these instructions to which you referred yesterday in your answer to Judge Orie's question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, there is apparently some difficulties in answering the question. I think, yesterday, the witness testified about what they were supposed to do with civilians, which certainly not did reflect clearly what is in the Geneva Conventions; that is, to get them all together, et cetera. So would be please be more specific and refer to specific portions of his answer, and then try to relate that in more detail, rather than to make it one, more or less, composite matter. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just going to use verbatim his statement from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, the statement you made yesterday was: "We were issued brief instructions relating to the civilian population, to the effect that their security should be ensured and that casualties should be prevented in the course of the military operation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please put to the witness the totality of what he said about what should happen to the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think there was more. Let me just check. Could you give me a reference of yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Page 2940, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to open it. One second. Yes. I have only the now the final numbering which is a bit off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It must be somewhere 2903 or 4, then. If you would give me one or two words.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "Instructions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We pulled it up as page 2940, line 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness explained that they had to transport the civilians as well. So that was a more -- there was more than just taking care that nothing would happen to them. And if would you please include that in your question, and say, "The instructions we referred to yesterday including this and this and this was that ...", then I think it could create less confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think our position, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or to split it up, that 's fine as well; but include that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can I just ask him the first question that I had asked, and then I will follow up with your question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The question -- my question was: You said you were issued brief instructions relating to the civilian population, to the effect that their security should be ensured. Who issued those instructions?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were verbal instructions given by the platoon commander at Jadrija; plus, we didn't even know then that we were going into Operation Storm. Most of these instructions had to do with the treatment of civilians and transports, as we were moving, as we were already in the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, second, I believe what Judge Orie is referring to is this which would be a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, perhaps, to be more precise, you were referring to instructions of a rather abstract nature. I was referring to part of instructions which are more of a concrete nature. The first is: Take care that nothing happens. The second is: Take them here or take them there, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What I'll getting to next, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- stand before the house and take care that no one enters. That is concrete and abstract. That is what is it bothering me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's what my next question was going to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You said that: "The troops who were advancing on the territory ..." -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is page 2939, starting at line 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "The troops who were advancing on the territory were secure so that all civilians we encountered would be transported to these collection centres." Now, who issued the instructions to transport civilians to the collection centres?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of the these instructions from other soldiers, when the one 113th Sibenik Brigade officially entered Djevrska at 7.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So this was not part of the instructions that you received from the platoon commander, which you just reference earlier, prior to Operation Storm. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think Mr. Misetic used a word "prior to Operation Storm," but I cannot recall the witness ever saying that he received any instructions prior to Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He just said that it -- that at their gathering place is when a platoon commander, and I can pull up and show it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: He just refers to the place Jadrija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify that. Mr. Gojanovic, when you gave the answer that you received verbal instructions from a platoon commander at Jadrija. Jadrija, was that the meeting point prior to going into Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And this instruction that you refer to was given prior to Operation Storm. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instruction that I mentioned was issued in a very narrow sense before the beginning of the operation, when we didn't even know where we were headed or what we were supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could move on to the next topic -- oh, sorry. I need to marked for identification the order of General Gotovina, at least the portion of the order -- the attack order of the 2nd of August, and ask that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D201, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D201 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 8 of your 2005 statement. On page 6 of the English version, you talk about the following event: "Because the 113th had moved slower than was necessary, after the success of taking Djevrska, seven volunteers, including myself, spent one night in the town. The volunteers also included three conscripts. During that night, we searched the whole of the town."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you would be so kind as to pull up 1D22-0060. This is the statement given to the Gotovina Defence by Mr. Josip Elez, who was a company commander within the 1st Battalion of the 113th Brigade, given 8 May 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard the name Josip Elez before?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The first paragraph, he says: "This is a voluntarily statement concerning my participation in Operation Storm, during which time I was company commander within the 1st Battalion of the 113th Guards Brigade." And in the fourth paragraph, he says: "5 August 1995, we seized Gracac and advanced via Pekovica, Kula, Zdrapanja, Vacana, to Bribriska Glava, where the command of the 2nd Djevrska Brigade of the so-called ARSK was located. In the evening, seven of us, the late Zivko Baric, Ratko Despot..." Despot, by the way, is the name you gave us this morning of the individual. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Da [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "... Miljenko Zivkovic, Tihomir Mis, two conscripts and myself." Then: "When we entered the village of Djevrska at approximately 2100 hours, I am positive that Vladimir Gojanovic was not with us." Now just to clarify, Ratko Despot is the HV soldier of Serbian ethnicity to whom you referred to this morning. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you referred to someone where you said his nickname was Mis, or Mouse. Could it be that it was not his nickname but his surname?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I won't know that. My conclusions was this was his nickname because I had never heard of "Mis" as a surname before. It was my impression that Ratko Despot and Mis were active soldiers of the 113th Sibenik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is it possible, sir, that you were not one of the seven people who entered Djevrska and spent the night there on the 5th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same procedure, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D202, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just an a point of clarification, Mr. Gojanovic, in these statements, you have seen references to the village of Gracac. In that area of responsibility, is there a village called "Gracac" which is different from the town of Gracac.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that there is a village called Gracac and that it is very close to Sonkovici, which is at an elevated position above the main road where the attack -- the way the attack, the axis of the attack evolved on the first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Same paragraph of your statement, paragraph 8, at the beginning of the paragraph, you say: "After we captured the village of Sonkovici and the rest of our battalion followed us, I climbed on top of a tank with about six other soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you would please --first, let's call up 1D22-0280.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This morning, I asked you if you could identify any one of these six by name. You gave me the last name of that Zafranovic. I'm going to show you a statement to the General Gotovina Defence by an individual whose last name is Zafranovic, first name of Davor. The statement is given 12 May 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Page 2, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2: "I was mobilised on 4 August 1995 for the Operation Storm. I was also a member of the 113th Brigade in 1993/1992. I served as an infantry soldier in the infantry company." Paragraph 5: "I was a member of the 113th Brigade, 3rd Infantry Battalion, S Company. We all were reserve soldiers and were mobilised for the purpose of Operation Storm. The commander of my company was Darko Djaja. The deputy commander was Srecko Grubisic. "When we arrived in our starting point, we were ten infantry soldiers. We joined in the support of a tank. The commander of the tank was Radoslav Juricev, Sudac. Out of the ten of us who had arrived, five went with commander Juricev. The other five went on a tank to Gornje Bicine. The tank that Sudac was driving set out at Janko's house." I note in your statement, sir, you also make a reference to Janko's House.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will move on, and one of my colleagues are find the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Continuing on at paragraph 7: "After two kilometres, we took off the tank because there were many mines that had to be cleared." Paragraph 8: "I know the persons who joined the first and the second tank. I knew them from earlier. Personally, I do not recall that Vladimir Gojanovic was with us. I would have recognised him if he had been with us." Paragraph 11 : "I do not recall having met Vladimir Gojanovic during Operation Storm. I am absolutely certain that he was not with me on the tank. That was under the command of Sudac, and it set out for its task at Janko's house."
